Listen, and judge how calmly I tell you this. I loved the old man who lived with me. He never hurt me, and I wanted none of his money. But a cloudy film covered his pale blue eye. That vulture's eye made my blood turn cold. I had to get free of it.

last_attempts_log.asr_text: At midnight, for seven nights, I slowly opened his door. You should have seen my patience. He never even moved. Then I let one thin ray escape from my lantern, but I always found that eye shut. I could not act. I hated his eye, not him. Every morning, I kindly asked about his night's sleep. On night eight, I almost laughed at my own cleverness. Then my thumb slipped on the catch of my lantern.

last_attempts_log.asr_text: For an hour, he sat listening while I stood completely still. Finally, he groaned softly, in fear, not pain. I knew that sound well. I opened the lantern's cover, sending light onto his eye. It was completely open now. I heard low, quick beats, like a watch wrapped in cotton. His heart grew faster and louder. What if a neighbor heard? I rushed at him, and he gave one scream. I pulled him down and covered him with the heavy bed. Finally, his heart stopped, and I could feel no pulse. I hid his body under three floorboards, then replaced them exactly. You could search all night and find no mark. At four that morning, three police officers arrived and knocked. A neighbor had heard a scream from the house.

last_attempts_log.asr_text: I welcomed them and blamed my scream on a bad dream. I said the old man was away in the country. After showing every room, I brought chairs into his bedroom. You see, I sat right above the body without fear. They talked in a friendly way while I smiled. My head started hurting and I heard a ringing sound. No, it was that low, quick beating once again. I raised my voice, but the beating grew louder, too. I walked about and scraped my chair across the floorboards. They went on talking and smiling as before. The sound kept growing louder and louder. Could you bear that? They heard and knew. They were laughing at me. I could not stand any more. I killed him, I screamed. Pull up the floorboards here. That is the beating of his horrible heart.
